device.name: Blackmagic Cinema Cameras with Bluetooth
device.notes:
Direct BLE remote control for Blackmagic bodies that document Bluetooth. The current Pocket Cinema Camera 4K, 6K G2 and 6K Pro advertise this capability; do not infer it on another body merely because the shared SDI Camera Control protocol lists its parameters. BLE carries control and status, not preview video, recording media or firmware images.
Read Camera Model and Protocol Version before enabling a command. The Camera 4.9-era gain parameter (group 1, parameter 1), later signed-dB gain (parameter 13), and ISO (parameter 14) are different surfaces, not aliases to try blindly. A lens or media parameter also requires the corresponding hardware and current camera mode.

openness.notes: Blackmagic publishes the wire protocol. The public coral serializer and Rust client are corroboration only; no vendor app internals were used.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: No separate pairing-button procedure is documented. Connect and write an encrypted characteristic; the camera then displays the PIN.

exclusivity.recovery: Close other control apps. If a previously paired host cannot use an encrypted characteristic, forget only that stale host/camera bond and pair again rather than resetting camera settings.

pairing.notes: Device Information and Device Name are not stated to be encrypted; Outgoing/Incoming Camera Control, Timecode and Camera Status require the bond. Seeing the GATT table without using those characteristics is not a successful control session.

pin.notes: Shown in the camera's Bluetooth Setup menu when an encrypted write initiates bonding.

unpair.notes: The public protocol defines no camera-side unpair command or menu procedure.

issued_to_client: The host/camera bond created by the OS Bluetooth stack
credentials.notes: The six-digit PIN is displayed for the current pairing attempt and is not a reusable credential to record. Never log the PIN or bond keys.
stored_on_device: Bluetooth bond material and the client-facing camera name
Camera settings and any parameter state sent over CCU

factory_reset.description: Do not substitute a camera settings reset for a documented Bluetooth reset. The Bluetooth Setup menu and the host's own bond list are the first places to inspect when moving a second-hand camera.
factory_reset.effect: Not established. The developer protocol does not define a reset or unpair operation, and no evidence here says which bonds, names or camera settings a camera-menu reset would clear.

methods.description: Discover the vendor service, connect, subscribe, and initiate bonding with an encrypted-characteristic write. The camera supplies a fresh six-digit PIN in its Bluetooth Setup menu.

steps.action: Power the camera and leave its Bluetooth Setup menu reachable.
Scan for the vendor service and connect to the intended camera.
Read Camera Model and Protocol Version; stop if the body is not one the client supports.
Subscribe to Incoming Camera Control, Camera Status and Timecode before sending commands.
Write Camera Power On (01) to Camera Status, or another safe encrypted write, to initiate bonding.
Read the six-digit PIN shown in the camera's Bluetooth Setup menu and enter it in the host prompt.
steps.expect: The host stores a bond and encrypted reads, writes and notifications become usable.

steps.action: Wait for Camera Status versions-verified and initial-payload flags before treating the parameter cache as ready.
steps.expect: Camera Ready (0x20) is set, or a bounded wait fails visibly.

setup.notes: No Wi-Fi or cloud provisioning exists. Pairing is a separate recurring requirement: an encrypted-control client must complete the camera's six-digit bonding flow before use.

rejoin.notes: There is no network membership. A replacement central discovers the service and bonds again; an old central merely needs its stored bond.

steps.action: Close other camera-control clients, rediscover the vendor service, and repeat the six-digit bond flow if this host has no valid bond.

evidence.documentation_review: Blackmagic Camera Control (created 2025-08-04): SDI protocol pages 96-105 for the header, types, alignment, parameter ranges and examples; Bluetooth pages 109-110 for GATT, six-digit pairing, status and timecode. The March 2025 Pocket manual and current product page establish only the named Pocket models' Bluetooth feature. coral/blackmagic-camera-protocol at 21125e3b52ee30030452e571d8e4e215df44bbe4 and coral/blackmagic-camera-control at 46cb0fa63e2e8fb83116efccebfcb4f9b66be630 cross-check UUIDs, LE encoding, the eight-byte serializer and service-filtered discovery.
evidence.open_questions: Protocol Version's wire encoding and per-body feature mapping; exact connection/bond limits and unpair route; notification boundaries; GATT properties on each body; firmware transport and recovery; which commands are accepted by each lens and camera mode.

enter.notes: The BLE Camera Control service defines no bootloader entry or image transfer. Do not treat it as a DFU service.

initialization.notes: Subscribe before the first Outgoing Camera Control write.
Status flags also report pairing and initial-cache progress.
Use the returned model for the first feature gate.
Use the returned CCU version for the second feature gate; its byte encoding is not specified by the manual.

initialization.description: On an unbonded host, an encrypted write starts the six-digit pairing flow. Do not issue a recording or configuration command as the pairing probe; Camera Power On (01) is the manual's example, and even that should be used only when power-on is acceptable.

CCU_Command.description: One SDI Camera Control command 0 change-configuration packet as carried over BLE. All multibyte numeric elements are little-endian. Data length is the length byte minus four; total storage is rounded up to four bytes.

fields.description: Four command bytes plus payload length; excludes the three-byte outer header, reserved byte and padding.
fields.name: command_length

fields.description: 0 for change configuration; ignore unknown IDs.
fields.name: command_id

fields.description: Integral number of elements of data_type; actual width is command_length - 4. At most 56 bytes so the complete aligned packet stays within 64 bytes.
fields.name: data

fields.description: Zero to three zero bytes so (8 + data width) is divisible by four; padding is excluded from command_length.
fields.name: padding

parse_rules: Require at least eight bytes and 4 <= command_length <= 60. The complete aligned packet is 4 + command_length plus padding and must not exceed 64 bytes.
Let n = command_length - 4. Require n bytes at offset 8, then skip (- (8 + n)) mod 4 alignment bytes; require those bytes to be zero.
If command_id is not 0, skip the whole aligned envelope WITHOUT decoding it as command 0. Unknown IDs are not errors by themselves; length and padding are the only safe dispatch facts.

Data types 129-255 and operation types 128-255 are vendor-specific: skip the aligned envelope without typed-decoding it. Only command 0 with known types/operations is decoded further. Reserved types 6-127 and operations 2-127 remain invalid for this spec.
A void trigger has n = 0. A boolean has one byte, with zero false and nonzero true. int8/int16/int32/int64 elements are signed; strings have no NUL.
Fixed16 is signed int16 LE divided by 2048. Offset operation 1 is invalid for void; a nonzero boolean offset toggles.

Camera_Status.description: Bitmask in the one-byte encrypted Camera Status characteristic.
parse_rules: These are bits, not mutually exclusive enum values. Wait for versions-verified and initial-payload before using the initial parameter cache; Camera Ready is the preferred final signal.

rules: Establish that the runtime model is a body documented to expose Bluetooth before offering any control.
Use group 1 parameter 1 only for the Camera 4.9-era gain surface. Use parameters 13/14 only when the body/version supports dB gain/ISO; the manual does not provide their introduction versions.
Do not map the 2021 community JSON parameter table onto a newer body without the current official table and a runtime version check.
Treat the initial Incoming Camera Control payload and Camera Status ready flags as capability/state evidence, not proof that a write is safe in the current mode.

receive_reassembly.notes: This is a defensive client rule, not a claim that every firmware splits notifications the same way. Buffer a notification stream per connection. Parse each complete aligned CCU packet with payload_formats.CCU_Command; a new packet may follow immediately. Keep a short trailing fragment for the next notification. If a length or element width is impossible, drop the buffered stream rather than scanning for a magic byte that does not exist. Reconnect on persistent desynchronization. Do not concatenate unrelated writes and assume the camera accepts SDI's 255-byte VANC grouping limit as a BLE MTU guarantee. Unknown command IDs and vendor-specific data/operation ranges are skipped by aligned length, never decoded as command 0; only known command-0 types and operations are typed-decoded.

test_vectors.notes: Official Blackmagic manual examples; destination changed to 255 only where the spec's command uses broadcast. scripts/test_blackmagic_cinema_cameras.py independently rebuilds and parses them.

vendor_specific_envelopes_followed_by_kn.rule: The first three are skipped by aligned length; the last is decoded as command 0. Unknown command ID 0x81 with reserved type 6/operation 2 is also skipped, not rejected as command 0.

type_widths.fixed16_formula: decoded = signed_int16_le / 2048; encode nearest representable integer, then apply the parameter's valid range
type_widths.string: remaining data length; UTF-8, no terminator

remaining_unknowns: Protocol Version width, byte order/text encoding and a trustworthy per-model version-to-feature matrix.
BLE notification fragmentation/coalescing and negotiated-MTU behavior on real bodies.
Maximum simultaneous centrals and bonds, and a camera-side unpair/reset procedure.
Exact firmware-era introduction of dB gain (1.13), ISO (1.14) and other newer parameters; do not infer it from the 2021 JSON map.
Which Pocket and other Bluetooth bodies accept each lens, transport, media and display command in each mode.
Firmware update transport, image signing, entry and interrupted-update recovery; none is defined by this BLE protocol.
The generic schema has no signed-5.11 scalar type, so fixed16 commands use int16 with scale 1/2048 and a custom aligned-command handler for receive/reassembly.

characteristics.name: Camera Manufacturer
characteristics.notes: UTF-8 text; Blackmagic documents the value 'Blackmagic Design'.

characteristics.name: Camera Model
characteristics.notes: UTF-8 model string, for example 'URSA Mini Pro'. Use this rather than guessing from the advertised name.

instantaneous_autofocus.description: Lens group 0, parameter 1, void/boolean type 0, assign operation 0. Vendor example addressed to camera 4; destination 255 broadcasts.

offset_zebra_level.description: Display 4.2, fixed16 offset operation 1. The example adds 0.15; offsets are signed and clamped by the camera.

offset.description: Signed fixed16 delta; encode round(delta * 2048). Use small deliberate changes.

optical_stabilisation_off.description: Lens 0.6, boolean false, padded to 12 bytes. Requires a lens that supports OIS.

optical_stabilisation_on.description: Lens 0.6, boolean true, with three alignment zeros. Requires a lens that supports OIS.

set_exposure_us.description: Video 1.5, signed int32 LE exposure in microseconds, valid range 1..42000. Vendor's 10000 us example is in protocol_details.test_vectors.

set_focus.description: Lens 0.0, signed 5.11 fixed16 little-endian: 0.0 near through 1.0 far. Requires a controllable lens.

focus.description: Decoded 0.0..1.0; encode round(value * 2048) as signed 16-bit LE. The two zeros after the parameter are padding.

set_gain_db.description: Video 1.13, signed int8 gain in dB plus three padding zeros. Parameter introduction/version is not specified; enable only when model/version evidence supports it.

set_iso.description: Video 1.14, signed int32 LE ISO. Gate on model/version; do not send to a Camera 4.9-era gain-only implementation.

set_legacy_gain.description: Video 1.1, Camera 4.9-era gain multiplier as int8 plus three padding zeros. Gate on model/version; never substitute this for dB gain or ISO.

set_manual_white_balance.description: Video 1.2: two signed int16 LE values, color temperature then tint; exactly four payload bytes, no trailing padding.

characteristics.name: Outgoing Camera Control
characteristics.notes: Host-to-camera CCU messages. The pinned Rust client writes without response; check the actual properties on the body/firmware. Every value below includes the eight-byte header, data and implicit zero padding to a four-byte boundary. The length byte is data length + 4, not total packet length and not padding-inclusive.

characteristics.name: Incoming Camera Control
characteristics.notes: Camera-to-host CCU messages with the same framing. Unknown command IDs must be skipped using length plus alignment, not rejected by assuming a fixed parameter table. Notification fragmentation and coalescing are not specified; protocol_details.receive_reassembly is the defensive parser to use without inventing a packet delimiter.

characteristics.name: Timecode
characteristics.notes: Four-byte BCD HHMMSSFF; the manual's numeric example 0x09125310 means 09:12:53:10 and calls the last component mm (frames in this context). It does not state the characteristic's byte order, so retain the raw bytes and establish that order on hardware rather than assuming either endianness.

power_off.advanced_reason: Powering off can interrupt recording or an in-progress write to camera media. Confirm the camera is idle first; recovery is to power it on locally or with 01.
power_off.description: Write 00 to power a connected camera off.

power_on.description: Write 01 to power a connected camera on. Also the manual's example of an encrypted write that initiates bonding.

characteristics.name: Device Name
characteristics.notes: UTF-8 without a terminator, maximum 32 characters. This is the name displayed in the camera's Bluetooth Setup menu, not a CCU string command.

characteristics.name: Protocol Version
characteristics.notes: Read before feature selection. The manual does not state width, byte order or text encoding; retain the raw value and use only a version mapping established for that body.
